observation.what_happens: An orange block hangs from a vertical spring fixed to an overhead support and oscillates up and down. The block starts near its lowest position and continues bouncing freely for the whole clip.

reasoning: The s channel shows ~0.6 s period vertical oscillation starting large (~250 pix) and decaying to ~100 pix, so a 1-D spring-mass oscillator around an equilibrium. Candidates go from ideal to viscous-damped to viscous plus quadratic air drag and cubic stiffness to test decay law and large-amplitude effects on the unseen tail.

critique.finding: The block bounces around {s_eq} with pace {w} slowed by {gamma} and a stiffness shift {alpha} plus a repeating push {F_drive} at {w_drive}. It only partly captures the motion and leaves a slow drift in its misses.
critique.headline: Hanging spring block bounces with unexplained extra push
critique.revision_idea: Let the support equilibrium drift slowly as the mount settles under load. Early misses sit low and late misses sit high, which a fixed equilibrium plus steady push cannot explain.
critique.why_it_won: It adds cubic stiffness and a repeating push that follows the extra wobble that plain damped and ideal springs cannot follow.

headline: A law drawn by public randomness, its round named before it existed: a lopsided spring with dry friction and a drive. The drive was found, added by code at the unexplained residual frequency; the stiffness and the friction were not.
finding: The block bounces around about 103 pix with pace about 11 1/s slowed by about 0.042 1/s and a stiffness shift about -0.0025 1/(s²·pix²) plus a repeating push about 3930 px/s² at about 16 rad/s. It only partly captures the motion and leaves a slow drift in its misses.

eyeball.confidence: low - single still impression of damped vertical spring-mass, no measured pixel time-series available
eyeball.law_in_words: vertical position s in pixels obeys damped spring-mass s_double_dot = -w^2*(s - s_eq) - gamma*s_dot - q*abs(s_dot)*s_dot - alpha*(s - s_eq)^3 + F_drive*cos(w_drive*t + phi_drive) with w = sqrt(k/m)

truth.note: This clip was rendered from a law drawn by public randomness (drand round 6605631). The round was named in 3bc0190 and pushed before it existed; the law's SHA-256 was pushed in d846c66 before the clip was rendered; the run used commit 0b852c8 on a clean tree; the law was revealed in b1902a4. Missed under the rule, with the drive found. The drawn law was a lopsided spring with dry (Coulomb) friction and a periodic drive at 16.30 rad/s. The misses of Muse Spark's best law peaked at 16.40 rad/s, 123 times the noise, labelled unexplained, and code added that law plus a drive started there. That law won: drive frequency 16.36 ± 0.19 rad/s against 16.30 (0.3σ), drive strength 4.7 ± 1.1 m/s² against 4.38, natural frequency 10.67 ± 0.22 against 10.50. But its cubic term (softening, 2.8σ) stands where the drawn stiffness is lopsided, and both its damping terms are within 2σ of zero where dry friction was drawn. Muse Wonder wrote a drive too, with a drifting rest point; it ranked second. The winner misses the unseen frames by 51 times the noise. With no ruler found, lengths are in pixels; true values in pixels use the render's own scale.

si.scale: the render's own scale, 0.00119 m per pixel (orthographic camera)

drawn.equation: x'' = -(k/m) x - (k2/m) x^2 - mu sign(x') + F0 cos(wd t)
drawn.x: displacement below the resting point (m, down positive); t from release

k2.rule: k2 A / k uniform in [0.2, 0.45], stiffer stretched (drawn 0.319)

mu.rule: the swing dies in N half cycles, N uniform in [10, 16] (drawn 11.32); mu = w0^2 A / (2N)

F0.rule: F0 / |w0^2 - wd^2| = share of A uniform in [0.15, 0.35] (drawn 0.250)

wd.rule: wd / w0 uniform in [0.55, 0.8] or [1.25, 1.6], each half the time (drawn 1.551)

sealed.narration: a block on a spring, filmed from the side
sealed.rule: found only if the winner's term set equals the drawn term set, a fitted term whose constant is within 2σ of zero counting as absent, and every shared constant is within 2σ of the drawn value
sealed.terms: winner (code: Muse Spark's law plus a drive at the unexplained residual peak): linear (w), viscous γ = 0.04 ± 1.1 (0.0σ, absent), quadratic q = 0.0011 ± 0.0015 (0.7σ, absent), cubic α = −0.0025 ± 0.0009 (2.8σ, present), drive F = 3933 ± 890 px/s² (4.4σ, present) at ω_d = 16.36 ± 0.19; drawn: linear, quadratic (lopsided), Coulomb, drive. Term sets differ: cubic where lopsided was drawn, and no damping where Coulomb was drawn.

spectrumAtScoring.summary: Residual spectrum of “Damped spring with air drag and cubic stiffness” on the fitted frames (its misses, fitted as sinusoids one at a time, strongest first): strongest at ω = 16.40 rad/s (period 0.383 s), amplitude 123 × the noise (21.3 px in s): UNEXPLAINED, neither the motion's own frequency nor a harmonic of it; a periodic drive at this frequency is worth testing, and the held-out frames will reject one that is not there; next at ω = 5.81 rad/s (period 1.081 s), amplitude 51.9 × the noise (8.98 px in s): UNEXPLAINED, neither the motion's own frequency nor a harmonic of it; a periodic drive at this frequency is worth testing, and the held-out frames will reject one that is not there; next at ω = 1.25 rad/s (period 5.037 s), amplitude 49.7 × the noise (8.60 px in s): under two cycles in the fitted 4.5 s, a slow drift, not resolvable as a periodic force. The motion's own frequency is 10.17 rad/s.
